description.narrative: ADB and the Government of Punjab in India are working together to improve the state's finances so that it can better deliver government services. The state is undertaking a comprehensive fiscal consolidation program to free up money that can be spent on health, education, power, and public works. The program is also addressing environmental issues through improved targeting of free power for irrigation. The program is expected to create adequate fiscal space for augmenting development spending in the state.

description.narrative: Larger and sustainable fiscal space in the state government

By FY2016 Own-tax revenue is at least 9% of GSDP (Baseline: 7.9% in FY2012). Progress/Status: Ratio of own-tax revenue to GSDP stagnated at about 7% from FY2012 until FY2017RE. It is projected to reach 8.5% in FY2018BE with the implementation of the goods and services tax across India. Data Source: Finance accounts and budget documents of GOP Baseline value: 7.9

Revenue deficit contained at around 0.7% of GSDP by FY2016 (Baseline: actual revenue deficit to GSDP ratio of 2.6% of GSDP in FY2012) Progress/Status: The ratio of current deficit to GSDP was brought down to 2.2% in FY2016 from 2.6 in FY2012. The ration will increase to 2.7% in FY2017RE. Data Source: Finance accounts and budget documents of GOP Baseline value: 2.6
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. Improved capacity for fiscal management Indicator: By FY2016 Major public investment approvals of GOP are vetted by the FPMU (Baseline: FPMU does not exist). Progress/Status: Achieved. FPMU was set up under the first-tranche policy action no. 2 to approve public investment by the Government of Punjab. Data Source: Notifications and reports from the Finance Department Baseline value: 0 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2016 Target value: 0

Output: 1. Improved capacity for fiscal management Indicator: Not more than 3%-4% discrepancies between estimated (budgeted) and actual own-tax revenue and total expenditure (excluding debt servicing payments) (Baseline: 5% for own-tax revenue and 12.8% for total expenditure in FY2012) Progress/Status: Not achieved. During the FY2013-FY2016, on average, the discrepancy between estimated and actual own-tax revenue was 10%, and 10.8% in the case of total expenditure, missing the target of 3%-4%. (Source: Government of Punjab. Budget at a Glance of various years). Data Source: Finance accounts and budget documents of GOP Baseline value: 5 Baseline value: 5 Target year: 2016 Target value: 4

Output: 1. Improved capacity for fiscal management Indicator: The cash management system is developed and operational (Baseline: system is currently not in place). Progress/Status: Achieved. Integrated financial management system was implemented by the Finance Department for treasury cash forecasting and debt management as per third-tranche policy action no. 20. Data Source: Notifications and reports from the Finance Department Baseline value: 0 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2016 Target value: 0

Output: 1. Improved capacity for fiscal management Indicator: Well-documented gender responsive MTEFs in place for major spending departments (Baseline: no MTEF in place) Progress/Status: Achieved. Gender-responsive medium-term expenditure frameworks for health, education, power, and public works departments were established as per third-tranche policy action no. 18. Data Source: Budget documents of GOP Baseline value: 0 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2016 Target value: 0

Output: 2. Rationalized expenditure focusing on power subsidies Indicator: By FY2016 Agricultural power supply data disaggregated at feeder levels and documented (Baseline: not available). Progress/Status: Achieved. PSPCL completed 100% feeder metering under first-tranche policy action no. 5. Data Source: Annual report of PSPCL Baseline value: 0 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2016 Target value: 0

Output: 2. Rationalized expenditure focusing on power subsidies Indicator: Power subsidy per hectare of gross cropped area declines by at least 4% over no reform scenario (No reform scenario: Rs11,920 in FY2016). Progress/Status: Achieved. Actual power subsidy per hectare of gross cropped area decreased to Rs6,157 in FY2016. This is 48.3% lower than the FY2016 baseline under no-reform scenario, exceeding the target of at least 4% decline. Data Source: Annual report of PSPCL Baseline value: 11920 Baseline value: 11920 Target year: 2016 Target value: 4

Data Source: Notification from the Revenue Department Baseline value: 75 Baseline value: 75 Target year: 2016 Target value: 100
